records.title: fix(audit): resolve P0/P1 audit findings and modernize typing
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: The live audit (docs/PROJECT_FULL_AUDIT_BN.md) identified critical contract mismatches between VS Code model tiers and gateway routing policies, SDK 404s due to missing chat endpoints, and security exposures from hardcoded secrets and open interface bindings. records.title: feat(bridge): fix(hooks): close the single-quote fail-open hole in the pre-commit secret scanner (.githooks/pre-commit check 2). RCA: the delimiter bracket written as ["\x27] does NOT contain the single-quote in POSIX ERE - bracket expressions treat \x27 as four literal characters (backslash, x, 2, 7). Proven 3-axis on the deployed pattern: (1) single-quoted secret literals were NOT matched - a fail-open hole on the exact class the guard exists to stop, and single-quoted strings are ubiquitous in Python/JS; (2) x/2/7-delimited values WERE matched (accidental false-positive class); (3) double-quoted worked only via the plain quote char. Fix: bracket carries both literal quotes. Self-test extended S1-S5 -> S1-S7 pinning both directions. Refs #161. (bridge-20261017-hook-quote-class)
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: The pre-commit guard (landed 0ec0e44/#678 as the #161 shift-left poka-yoke) exists to stop raw credential literals from entering git history, but its delimiter bracket never contained the single-quote character: POSIX ERE bracket expressions interpret backslash escapes literally, so \x27 matched x/2/7/backslash instead of the quote. The result is a fail-open hole for single-quoted secrets - the most common quoting style in the languages this repo ships - plus a false-positive class for x/2/7-delimited values. Closing the hole in the guard itself is the root-cause fix; the two new self-test fixtures pin both directions so the class cannot regress silently (same fail-closed discipline the repo applied in #658 for the CI guards).
records.alternatives_rejected: - 1) Use -P (PCRE) for real \x27 semantics - rejected: GNU grep -P availability varies across runner images and the guard must stay portable POSIX sh/ERE per its own header contract. 2) Match unquoted 20+ char values too - rejected: would false-positive on legitimate identifiers/constants and train users to bypass with --no-verify; the guard targets quoted literals only. 3) Replace the grep with a python scanner - rejected: adds interpreter startup cost to every commit for a one-line pattern fix (P0 minimal elegance). 4) Report-only - rejected: this is a security guard with a proven fail-open hole; shipping the one-line fix with pinned self-tests is the smallest safe change.

Adding the alias is the smallest safe change that makes the criterion executable and true; it is mechanical, runtime-neutral, and keeps test:unit (the offline-safe matrix) as the target so bare checkouts without credentials still exit 0 via the documented env-skip contract.

records.title: perf(infra): optimize landing workflow triggers to run only on active PRs (#688)
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: Whenever commits land on `main` (either direct pushes or post-merge commits), `CI — Open Unified Pipeline` executes and subsequently fires `landing.yml`. Without a trigger event filter, `landing.yml` spun up an Ubuntu runner and acquired the exclusive `landing-merge-open` concurrency lock only to discover no open PR exists and exit. During rapid consecutive landings, this caused runners to queue for up to 10-11 minutes behind active merges. Filtering for `github.event.workflow_run.event == 'pull_request'` ensures landing only runs when an active PR has finished its unified CI suite.
records.alternatives_rejected: - Removing `workflow_run` entirely and relying only on manual dispatch: Rejected because it breaks zero-admin autonomous landing of contributor PRs.

records.title: feat(infra): enforce LF line endings on git hooks via .gitattributes (Refs #161)

Placing .gitattributes ensures git always preserves LF line endings for hooks and shell scripts across all developer and CI environments.
records.alternatives_rejected: - Setting local git config only: rejected because it does not protect other developers, CI runners, or newly spawned agents on Windows.

records.title: feat(infra): add actionable agent guidance box to pre-commit and post-commit hook (Refs #161)

Adding an explicit, non-interactive guidance box (telling the agent to run continuous_agent_loop.py --verify-only and re-check task contracts) prevents process freezes while providing immediate recovery directives. The post-commit hook reinforces the Dual-Rebase Mandate right after every successful local commit.
records.alternatives_rejected: - Running continuous_agent_loop.py inside pre-commit: rejected because the loop invokes git commit during Step 7, which would create an infinite recursive deadlock.

records.title: feat(infra): add pre-commit shift-left guard and dual-rebase mandate (Refs #161)
records.author: paykaribazaronline

Shift-left validation at the local pre-commit boundary eliminates broken commits before they enter git history. Dual-rebase guarantees branches are fresh both at branch creation time and right before push.
records.alternatives_rejected: - Running full federation test suite on every pre-commit: rejected because >30s commit latency harms developer flow; opted for <2s fast-path targeting staged files only (staged .ts in mcp-control-plane, staged .py py_compile, staged secrets, and stale-base check).

records.title: feat(bridge): audit(command): MiniRedis RESP parser returns garbage + webhook serve() ignores its port. RCA: dispatcher.py _command does ONE sock.recv(4096) and returns data.split(CRLF)[0] → GET reply '$5\r\nhello\r\n' returns the LENGTH PREFIX '$5' as the value (A/B proven: old code GET → '$5'; any real Redis value read is broken; KillSwitch.armed() only works by accident since any non-empty string is truthy). webhook_ingress.py serve(ingress, port) binds port 0 then assigns server.server_port AFTER bind → production serve(ingress, 8787) listens on a random ephemeral port (proven). Live-verified on main@4278d17. Dedup: no ticket. Optimal way: proper RESP reader for simple/error/int/bulk (dispatcher surface is SET/GET/DEL); bind_port parameter threaded into ThreadingHTTPServer. Recurrence prevention: behavioral proofs in CI-able form; truncated-read class eliminated at the parser. (bridge-20261017-audit-command-runtime)
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: why: the command satellite's Redis client returns the bulk length prefix ('5') instead of values — every GET is garbage — and the webhook runtime binds a random port while ignoring its port argument, so deployments are unreachable on the configured port.
records.alternatives_rejected: - alternatives_rejected: (a) using a full redis-py client — rejected: new dependency violates the seed's zero-dep design (P3 preserve working architecture); a correct RESP reader for the SET/GET/DEL surface is ~30 lines; (b) for webhooks, re-creating the server inside serve() — rejected: binding at construction keeps the factory testable; threading the port is the minimal change.

records.title: fix(mcp-tower): prevent unverified named viewer guests from failing closed on slot store unreachability
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: Unauthenticated named clients (such as web AI connectors presenting \?client=<name>\ without a secret bearer token) should operate strictly in the safe \iewer\ role. Previously, \src/index.ts\ created a \slotBinding\ purely because \session.slotId\ was populated by the fallback helper, which subsequently caused every JSON-RPC message in \/messages\ or \/mcp\ to run \^GssertSlotAuthorization()\. During an Upstash Redis outage, quota exhaustion, or network latency, the operational store became unverifiable, causing innocent anonymous viewers to fail closed with HTTP 403 Forbidden (\slot-store-unreachable\). By gating \slotBinding\ on \session.slotVerified\ and scoping operational store checks in \^GssertSlotAuthorization\ to real slot identities (\isSlotId(slotId)\), we preserve fail-closed security for real credentialed slots while ensuring public AI guests remain permanently resilient.
records.alternatives_rejected: - Disabling the operational store check entirely: rejected because Issue #48 requires fail-closed revocation for actual privileged credential-holding slots.

records.title: fix(bridge): add Closes keyword for work orders in auto_bridge_pr_opener (Closes #432)
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: Previously, `auto_bridge_pr_opener.py` only included `Refs #{wo_num}` in the PR body. GitHub only triggers automated issue closing when explicit closing keywords like `Closes #N` or `Fixes #N` are present in the final merge commit body. Adding `Closes #{wo_num}` ensures GitHub autonomously closes the work order issue as soon as the PR is squash-merged into `main`.
records.alternatives_rejected: - Leaving it as `Refs #{wo_num}` and relying on manual issue closures (violates Zero-Admin budget <= 0.01%).

records.title: feat(ingress): enforce Two-Tier Ingress Invariant — No Claim No Branch, No Branch No Push
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: Prevents orphan branches and unclaimed code pushes before they even leave the developer or agent workspace. Previously, `continuous_agent_loop.py` created branches locally before securing claims on GitHub, and `.githooks/pre-push` only checked base freshness without checking if the target issue was claimed. Enforcing *No Claim -> No Branch* in `step_4_branch` guarantees that no task branch can be checked out unless the issue claim is securely registered on GitHub. Enforcing *No Branch -> No Push* in `.githooks/pre-push` stops unauthorized pushes of issue branches at the terminal level before any bytes hit the remote.
records.alternatives_rejected: - Enforcing only at PR review time — rejected because orphan branches still accumulate on remote repositories (50+ bridge branches evidenced).

records.title: fix(ci): enforce mandatory Claim Gate & Knowledge Sharing Guard in pipeline.yml
records.author: paykaribazaronline
records.reflection_why: Enforces the constitutional requirement of AGENTS.md Step 4 (No claim, no work) at the CI level. Previously, external agents pushed branches and opened PRs without claiming issues, causing collisions and ghost PRs. Implementing zero-checkout `claim-guard` and `knowledge-sharing-guard` ensures every PR has an active claim on the target issue and preserves architectural decision rationale.
records.alternatives_rejected: - Server-side pre-receive push hook — rejected because GitHub Cloud does not support arbitrary server-side pre-receive hooks; client/CI gates at PR time are the fail-closed standard.
